# Intro
![](/images/linux_intermdiary.png){style="width:200px" fig-align="center"}

We have covered a small amount of Linux coding. This should be sufficient to carry out our future workshops but if you were to continue in bioinformatics we would recommend learning more advanced methods.

This section contains tutorials to introduce you to some more advanced linux coding techniques. These give you a quick overview and some examples. This will hopefully put you in a good position to allow you to learn these techniques in more depth outside of this workshop.

This section will all be run with the files in the directory __"~/Linux/advanced_practice/"__. Therefore ensure you are in this directory before running the examples. This contains fastq and txt files for 20 samples. Each sample contains a fastq file and a txt file for uncorrected and corrected reads. These fastq files are single ended (i.e. there are no reverse/R2 reads).

## Contents

The pages of this section are:

- [Wildcard characters](/advanced/wildcards.qmd): Characters that can represent other characters (e.g. `*`)
- [Redirection](/advanced/redirection.qmd): Redirecting the output of a command to a file (`>`)
- [Pipes](/advanced/pipes.qmd): Piping various commands together (`|`)
- [Regular expressions](/advanced/regular_expressions.qmd): Characters to match search patterns with finer control than wildcards
- [sed](/advanced/sed.qmd): A command that can substitute/replace text
- [Recap](/advanced/recap.qmd): Info on permissions and recap MCQs
- [Exercise](/advanced/advanced_practice_exercise.qmd): Tasks to complete base don the various advanced linux techniques learnt
